_pricing_note: RESOLVED 2026-09-04 via Microsoft support ticket API TrackingID#2608200050000071 — the previous belief here (pricing is unwritable for this account, leave it untouched) was WRONG and caused a real 'InvalidParameterValue: Base is not a valid PriceId' rejection on every submit-ms-store.ps1 PUT from 2026-08-20 onward. Microsoft's own Engineering Team confirmed: GET returns 'Base' as an internal sentinel that can NEVER be written back on PUT; PUT requires a concrete tier instead — for isAdvancedPricingModel=true accounts (WhisPaste's case) that means 'Free' or Tier1001+ (legacy Tier2-Tier96 are rejected for this pricing model). pricing.priceId must be present with a valid value in EVERY PUT (the classic Submission API does a full replacement) — omitting it silently defaults to Free. scripts/submit-ms-store.ps1 now reads default.PriceId from here, validates it, and writes it explicitly on every submission. Tier1037 = 3.49 EUR (Germany, WhisPaste's real live price, confirmed both in Partner Center > Pricing and availability's Base price field AND independently in the tier conversion CSV: Partner Center > Pricing and availability > 'Download this info (.csv)' under the price-tier table (the in-browser table itself renders the EUR column as a literal '...' for every row — a Partner Center display bug, not a data gap; the CSV is unaffected and is the reliable source). CORRECTION vs. the previous version of this note: the Tier1001+ range IS linear/predictable in this region (1012=0.99, 1013=1.09, ... +0.10 per tier up to at least 1044=4.19) — the earlier 'not guessable/non-linear' claim here was an unverified assumption, not a Microsoft statement; verify with the CSV before relying on the pattern outside this observed range, since Microsoft reserves the right to change conversion rates. Full trail: ~/.claude/infrastructure/microsoft-partner-center.md §12, docs/store-release.md.
